status: new failure class identified; Gate A still IN PROGRESS and unaccepted
scope: human panel test at maximum LFO speed with and without USB; one live Pi sample of the frozen device
firmware: V01G (usb-track 0.5, compact snapshots, no self-wake), unmodified since the compact-depth48 capture
human_protocol: Empty pattern/preset, SRC machine set to USB1, LFO destination TRX-B2 PTCH, speed multiplier 2000 (BPM multi), depth 5-10.
A: all cables to the Pi disconnected -> fully responsive, all controls smooth, no perceived lag.
B: reconnect the USB cable -> instant freeze; UI unresponsive for >13 minutes.
Earlier: pressing SPD to 2K while connected also froze it, and unplugging did not restore the UI within 1 minute.

findings.native_2k_is_cheap: With USB detached, the native LFO at maximum rate is free: no lag. Any 'the Digitakt cannot compute a 2 kHz LFO' explanation is excluded.
findings.freeze_survives_detach: Once frozen, removing the cable does not recover it, and re-attaching triggers it immediately. The permanent stop is tied to USB attachment/handling, not to sustained LFO cost.
findings.not_cpu_saturation: Last healthy values before death were small: ui gap max 34 ms, worker gap max 34 ms, batch 4 ms, guards 0. An overload degrades gradually; this stops atomically.
findings.device_side_dead: Digitakt-side counters stop: rx/sends/timer/block/seq all identical across 30 s of sampling (seq 42, block 238672, sends 11266). The remote diagnostic emitter itself stops, so the stall covers the whole native device, not only our worker.
findings.audio_lost: The Pi side reports gadget 0 / streaming false and underruns climbing, consistent with a stopped device. The frozen device is not sending PCM.
findings.no_hardware_fault: Pi stayed alive, answered HTTP, stayed at 54 C with no throttling. The earlier fresh Pi boot was a human restart, not a spontaneous reboot.

leading_hypothesis.name: irq-masked busy wait in the native USB-MIDI sender
leading_hypothesis.mechanism: fw_send() masks all interrupts (move.w #0x2700,%sr) across the call to 0x40004990. That routine contains two unbounded busy waits (wrap at 0x400049D0..D8, capacity at 0x400049FE..0x40004A0C) whose only drain is the completion callback 0x40004404 lowering 0x40610478. If a wait is entered, interrupts are already masked, so the drain can never run and the device hangs. The staging ring wraps every ~120 ms at the observed ~816 sends/s, so the condition is reached repeatedly.
leading_hypothesis.why_density_scales: The wrap probability and submission rate both rise with effective update rate, matching that 64/48 slowed and 2K froze.
leading_hypothesis.second_order: With the cable out the 256-record session ring fills in ~170 ms and latches fatal; that explains the lost audio but not the frozen UI.
leading_hypothesis.confidence: hypothesis, not proof: the busy-wait instructions and the masking are both source facts; that they coincided here is inferred from the failure signature.

alternate_hypotheses: Attach/enumeration path (dt1_transport_open / RX-slot replacement / chain_stock into the stock handler) rather than send volume.
ISR-context work: native_rx -> receive() -> sc_dev_receive_control and device_wakeup running at interrupt level.
Unmodelled divergence between the emulator's can_send thresholds and the real 0x40610478/0x4061047C state.

discriminating_test.procedure: USB attached, USB1 selected, LFO running at 2K with destination OFF (not routed to TRX-B2) so the hook emits nothing while the native LFO runs at full speed.
discriminating_test.if_responsive: send path/volume; fix in fw_send/can_send and worker batching.
discriminating_test.if_frozen: attach/enumeration or ISR-context path; search dt1_transport_open, native_rx, chain_stock.
discriminating_test.cost: ~30 s, no flash; power-cycle the Digitakt first

source_anchors.send: mods/usb-midi/usb_midi.c: fw_send() -> USB_SEND 0x40004990 inside the masked section

limits: Single human trial per condition; no repeated freeze to measure determinism.
No on-device trace of the hang: the remote emitter stops with the device, so the failing PC is not captured.
The LFO rate/depth were set by hand; no panel readback of symbolic speed 2000.
The 2K freeze is a stronger failure than the 64/48 'sluggish' complaint; whether they share one cause is unproven.
Pi 'gadget 0' was read from the status endpoint; the engine source for that field is not in this clone.
next: Run the discriminating test; if the masked-wait hypothesis survives, replace the masked send with a bounded, IRQ-enabled path and add a host regression that fails when a busy wait is entered with interrupts masked.
